name: Refraction Mastery
tagline: Advanced Refraction Techniques for the Optometrist
description: A 15-episode deep dive into the art and science of refraction — retinoscopy, cross cylinder, cycloplegia, and the difficult refractions that separate competent optometrists from great ones.

episodes.title: Streak Retinoscopy: Working Distance, Sleeve & Neutralisation
episodes.description:
Ever watched an optometrist sweep a streak of light across a patient's eye and wondered exactly what they're looking for? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down streak retinoscopy into its three essential pillars: working distance, sleeve position, and neutralisation — the concepts that separate a confident clinician from a confused one.

We start with working distance, explaining why sitting at 66 cm or 50 cm from your patient isn't arbitrary, and how forgetting the working distance correction can send every patient home with the wrong prescription. Next, we unpack sleeve position — what happens when the sleeve is up versus down, why the plane mirror setting is the go-to for most clinicians, and how a single accidental sleeve flip can make your reflex behave in completely baffling ways. Finally, we walk you through neutralisation, that satisfying moment when the reflex floods the pupil with a steady, brilliant glow and all movement disappears — and how experienced retincopists bracket the endpoint from both sides to confirm accuracy.

We also touch on how retinoscopy extends beyond sphere to detecting astigmatism across meridians, and how reflex quality can hint at deeper ocular conditions like cataracts or keratoconus.

Whether you're an optometry student preparing for clinical placements, a practitioner revisiting the fundamentals, or simply curious about how prescriptions are determined objectively, this episode gives you a clear, practical, and memorable guide to one of optometry's most powerful skills.

Listen now, and visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and clinical resources to sharpen your optometry knowledge.

episodes.title: The Jackson Cross Cylinder: Refining Cylinder Axis and Power Systematically
episodes.description: The two-step JCC technique — axis first, then power — and the common errors that produce an unreliable cylinder.

episodes.title: Duochrome and Binocular Balancing: Equalising the Final Endpoint
episodes.description: Using the duochrome (red-green) test correctly, the "leave them on the green" rule, and prism dissociation for binocular balance.

episodes.title: Cycloplegic Refraction: Indications, Agents, and Interpretation
episodes.description: When cycloplegia is mandatory (children, hyperopes, suspected spasm), choosing cyclopentolate vs atropine, and interpreting the cycloplegic vs manifest difference.

episodes.title: Refracting the Pseudophakic Patient: IOL Power and Surprise Refractions
episodes.description: Why some cataract patients end up myopic or hyperopic after surgery, refracting through a multifocal IOL, and managing the unhappy post-op patient.

episodes.title: Refracting the Post-Refractive-Surgery Patient: LASIK, PRK, and RK
episodes.description: Why standard keratometry fails after corneal refractive surgery, how to estimate corneal power for IOL calculations, and over-refraction techniques.

episodes.title: Over-Refraction with Contact Lenses: Spherical, Toric, and Scleral
episodes.description: When to over-refract rather than re-fit, how to apply a spherical over-refraction to a toric lens, and interpreting a scleral lens over-refraction.

episodes.title: Refracting Children: Attention, Fixation, and the Worth 4 Dot
episodes.description: Age-appropriate acuity tests (Teller, LEA, HOTV), maintaining attention, and when to trust a manifest vs cycloplegic result in a child.

episodes.title: Presbyopia: Measuring the Add and Selecting the Right Design
episodes.description: Measuring amplitude of accommodation, calculating the add for the patient's working distance, and matching the add to lifestyle (single vision, PAL, computer).

episodes.title: High Refractive Errors: Myopia Above -10.00 and Hyperopia Above +6.00
episodes.description: Optical consequences of high ametropia, minimising aniseikonia, lens material and design choices, and when contact lenses become the better option.

episodes.title: Anisometropia and Aniseikonia: When the Image Sizes Differ
episodes.description: Quantifying aniseikonia with the Awaya test, the "knapp's rule" for axial anisometropia, and strategies to minimise image size disparity.

episodes.title: Irregular Astigmatism: Keratoconus, Post-Graft, and Epikeratophakia
episodes.description: Detecting irregular astigmatism on refraction, when retinoscopy scissoring appears, and rigid gas permeable fitting principles for irregular corneas.

episodes.title: Astigmatic Dial and Fan-Block Techniques for Cylinder Determination
episodes.description: When the JCC is unreliable (low vision, poor attention), using the astigmatic dial and fan-block to determine cylinder axis and power.

episodes.title: Vertex Distance and Pantoscopic Tilt: Compensating the Final Rx
episodes.description: How vertex distance changes effective power in high Rx, converting spectacle to contact lens power, and the effect of pantoscopic tilt on cylinder.

episodes.title: Prescribed Prism: Decentration, Fresnel, and Ground-In Prism
episodes.description: Calculating prism by decentration using Prentice's rule, when to use a Fresnel press-on prism, and prescribing yoked prism for neurologic patients.
